_note: BIOLOGY ONLY. Compiled from general spearfishing-guide sources (not a validated regional survey), for tropical Indian Ocean reef fauna (Red Sea, East Africa, and the wider western Indian Ocean). Heavy overlap with the Indo-Pacific coral-triangle list (species_bali.json) is real, not a copy-paste error: several of these genera range continuously from East Africa to the Central Pacific. Depth, temperature, substrate and season of presence and how each species responds to water clarity. None of it is law, and critically: spearfishing is banned outright in the Maldives, which sits inside this biome's rough geographic footprint - this app has no way to know it has crossed into Maldivian waters specifically, so do not take this file's presence as any indication spearfishing is permitted at a given point.

species.note: Coral trout - holds tight to reef structure and holes, among the most prized reef fish across the whole Indo-Pacific including the Red Sea.
Bohar/two-spot red snapper - holds around reef structure and drop-offs; large individuals carry a real ciguatera risk in parts of this range.
GT - patrols reef edges and drop-offs across the entire Indo-Pacific from East Africa to the Central Pacific, the same species and behaviour as Hawaii's ulua and Bali's GT.
One of the most iconic Red Sea and Persian Gulf reef fish - sand and rubble patches near reef edges rather than deep in structure.
Cruises reef drop-offs in open water rather than holding tight to structure, common on outer reef edges across the Indo-Pacific.
Hangs mid-water near reef edges throughout this range, less structure-bound than the grouper and snapper on this list.

_legal_note: Legal rules live in legal/<JURISDICTION>.json and are merged in at run time. No legal pack exists for any western Indian Ocean jurisdiction, so this app will correctly show 'not researched' rather than any size or season claim. This is a coarse ocean-basin fallback, not a country-specific pack: it cannot distinguish Egypt from Kenya from the Maldives, and spearfishing is banned outright in the Maldives specifically.
